scenes.headline: How a model carries eight experts and pays for two
scenes.sub: Mixture of Experts, built from one MLP, a router and a sparse pass.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Pancake! A mixture of experts carries lots of parameters, but each token only pays for a slice of them. Let's build one.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Conditional computation: keep several expert MLPs, and let a tiny router pick two for each token. The rest sit idle for that token.
scenes.mark: a tiny router pick two for each token
scenes.say: The idea is conditional computation. Keep several expert networks, and let a tiny router pick two for each token. The rest sit idle.

steps.say: A router, just one linear layer, gives the token a score for each of eight experts.

steps.note: top-k, then softmax: sparse, and still trainable
steps.say: It keeps the top two scores and softmaxes them into weights. The other six become exactly zero, yet gradients still reach both winners.
Only those two experts run. Each is simply the feed-forward network the block already had.
Their outputs are scaled by the weights and added. That's the whole layer.

steps.label: Every expert on every token
steps.say: Now picture a row of tokens against eight experts. Weight every expert for every token, and they all run: an expensive ensemble, not a sparse model.

steps.label: Top-2: two lit per token
steps.say: Keep the top two per token, and most of the grid goes dark. That darkness is compute you're not spending.

items.say: The catch is collapse. An expert that wins early gets gradient, improves, and wins even more.
So the router adds learned noise, and borderline experts sometimes win.
And serious models add a balancing loss that charges for lopsided routing.

scenes.title: Mixtral 8x7B, the same recipe at scale
scenes.say: Mixtral uses exactly this setup. It holds forty-seven billion parameters, but each token touches about thirteen billion.

scenes.text: A model's parameter count and its per-token compute stop being the same number. The price is memory.
scenes.say: So a model's parameter count and its per-token compute stop being the same number. The price is memory: every expert stays loaded.

recap: An expert is the FFN you already had
A router runs the top two of eight
Noise and a balancing loss prevent collapse
scenes.say: To recap: experts are feed-forward networks, a router runs two of eight, and noise plus a balancing loss keep them all fed.
